text:
Minecraft has pumpkins, bowls, and 15 years of missed opportunity

To whom it may concern,

I write this as a plea of desperation, mere weeks before my 25th birthday.

The humble pumpkin was added to Minecraft in Java Edition Alpha v1.2.0 in 2010, and my nine-year-old self was delighted. As the years passed, more craftable items emerged from our orange friend. And yet, even then, I began to feel the cold fingers of existential dread tugging at my child-sized Creeper attire.
For although we were able to create soups and stews of many kinds, the transcendental ecstasy of pumpkin soup remained forever barred from my grasp.

For years, my tiny child mind, unburdened by the knowledge of dev teams, update cycles, and feature prioritisation, persevered. I tried a pumpkin and a bowl. I tried milk, pumpkin, and a bowl. I even turned to pumpkin seeds in a futile attempt to craft this long-denied delicacy.

But no.
Although the pumpkin was right there, the opportunity ripe, and my heart hopeful, pumpkin soup remained uncraftable.

Now I build temples and empires. I have seen civilisations rise and fall. I have watched dimensions appear out of thin air. I have sat in hobbit holes, witch’s hovels, and pristine cherry blossom cottages. Yet through it all, Steve has never once raised to his lips the wholesome, life-altering comfort of pumpkin soup.
And so I carry an emptiness. A quiet ache. The knowledge that my Minecraft experience has never reached its full potential for true, wholesome coziness.

Minecraft Dev Team, if you exist, somewhere in your sacred order of developers: I have lived in a pumpkin-soupless purgatory for over fifteen years.

As my brain reaches full maturation at the age of 25, I ask now, with the faint light of hope flickering within me:

Please.

Add pumpkin soup to Minecraft.

Still happy to see these added to the game regardless. The feature is looong overdue.
Edit: I normally agree that Minecraft shouldn’t feel too modern, but in this case I feel the art style is flexible enough to accommodate the feature without resembling a contemporary nylon bag with a zipper.

text:
My Idea For An End Update

An update to the End is one of the most in-demand and wanted updates in the Minecraft community, if not THE most. Here is my idea of what should happen.

  1. The End around the Ender Dragon is the same out to 5000 blocks. The only difference is smaller gaps, more blocks.
  2. Between 5000 and 10000 blocks, we see alien landscapes - strange blocks, flora and fauna, containers, with some different low level boss types both hostile and friendly. They drop things that we don't know we need yet, but we do. Probably don't aggro the friendlies though! We find recipes for the next step in inventory after enderchests.
  3. Between 10000 and 15000 blocks, we start to see the answer to the question "What do endermen do with all those blocks they pick up in the Overworld and the Nether?" Landscapes exist with random blocks everywhere, with a bit a sculk here and there, more as we get closer to 15000 blocks out. There are some odd End Cities here with new loot. Also, we see the first appearance of enderite, the next in the chain after wood/copper/iron/diamond/netherite.
  4. From 15000 blocks out and up, we see far more common sculk, with blocks that look like sensors, but different. When activated, they spawn what looks like baby Wardens, or four-legged Wardens. Or both. There are a few houses and other buildings, new loot, new spell books, etc. We also find teleportation keys, which we can use to teleport to markers that we've visited in every dimension.
  5. After 20000 blocks, it's almost totally solid sculk mountains (and not the experience giving kind, either). It's nearly impassable - you'd have to find secret doors, or have the absolute best loot in the game, or... some other way. However, in different places we see some maps. Those maps lead not to buried treasure, but to books. Guarded by bosses or tough mobs? You bet your ass, but the books contain recipes, one of which is VERY VERY IMPORTANT.
  6. Because it's a way to make a new lighter, enderite and steel. Hmmm... Wonder what it lights?

  7. It lights the giant portal in an Ancient City. Walking through an Ancient City portal leads to the End, a different place for every portal, but in an area past 20000 blocks from the center of the End, on the higher numbered side of the super tall sculk mountains.
  8. What's there? The home of the Wardens and of sculk. We find out where the Wardens came from (or at least, where they have been coming from recently). We find out why and how they broke through to the Overworld (probably the ancients, right?). We find out WHY the Endermen were gathering blocks from the Overworld and Nether - to try to stop the Sculk from spreading and replace it with regular blocks. We find out why the dragon was summoned - to keep the sculk and Wardens at bay.
But over time the Wardens and the Dragon reached a balance at around 5000 blocks out, caused by the Dragon burning out everything but chorus fruit. The Dragon cleared the area out to 5000 blocks, and the Endermen pulled up ender blocks and created the gaps.
  9. A future update could explore if the Wardens came from yet another place.

  10. Or, it could skip to the Nether and explain who or what created Piglins and Ghasts, who created all the bastions and fortresses and why, how come you can't sleep or use water in the Nether, and who is behind all of it.

text:
Hot take: I like copper tools

A lot of people have said that copper tools are not good because they aren't important for progression. Why would you make copper tools when you could just go straight to iron? I actually object to this. I don't think copper should be a tool for progression, but instead, a tool for not wasting your better tools. For instance, I recently have been terraforming and landscaping my base. It started out as a hobbit hole with a weird mossy swamp area (Not actually a swamp, just kind of looked like it).
I decided to start terraforming it, and taking moss out, and now it looks more like a front yard! The amount of terraforming I did was insane, and it was all thanks to copper. But why would I use copper to terraform when I have a literal diamond pickaxe? Well, in my opinion, diamond is a scarce resource. Yes, you might have a lot in the late game, but in the mid or early game, you don't have as much access to materials like diamond or iron.
Plus, you aren't going to be mining obsidian or diamonds when polishing the outside of your base, that is unless you are making a nether portal or something. Idk, I like copper as more of a filler tool than a progression tool. Let me know your thoughts!
Side note: Is it just me, or does stone mine faster than cobblestone? I feel like that's a bit counterintuitive, but I could just be hallucinating.

text:
I've finally opened my eyes to copper tools

When copper ore and it's respective blocks first came out, I didn't enjoy the idea of this new ore barely having much functionality compared to iron while still being so much more readily available when mining. On top of that, copper blocks just oxidize over time if not waxed, meaning the blocks I worked to make would simply discolor if I didn't take care of them quickly.
Then, it dawned on me. Iron is insanely useful and relatively valuable in the early to midgame, but iron tools do most of the same stuff as copper tools when you're just digging or mining regular blocks most of the time. Copper tools are perfect midgame throwaway options for when you're working on any large digging/mining project and still need more iron to save up for an anvil, hoppers, etc. Stuff like strip mining, terraforming, and collecting sand for glass come to mind.
Of course, I'd still bring an iron pick to a proper caving or mining sesh in order to ensure I can grab each ore I find, but the copper can still help save durability if I ever just need to break some stone.
How do you guys like copper tools? Does my stance on their relative uses in a survival world make sense? Also, what tips do you have regarding using copper decorative blocks when I eventually get to building a decent base in my world later on?

I hate that currently the only two options for finding the enchantment you’re looking for is gambling at the enchantment table or enslaving an entire hall of librarian villagers (the exception being the enchantments that you can only find in certain structures).

Right now there’s 80+ enchantments that you can obtain from librarians and the addition of new enchantment families only makes trying to find the right one being sold even more tedious and frustrating.
I think a very simple solution that many others have suggested would just be allowing us to choose the right enchantments we want from the table at the cost of possibly more xp or maybe even allowing us to unlock each enchantment after finding a book with that enchantment out in the wild. Obviously this isn’t a full proof idea because librarians would have to be reworked to provide their own value.
